front.title: Minimum Public Discovery Information: Requirements and Common Semantics

abstract.t:
The charter of the Discovery of Agents With Names (DAWN) working group asks it to specify the minimum public discovery information that a client obtains when it discovers an AI resource. An individual draft on DAWN terminology calls this Minimum Discoverable Information (MDI) but gives only examples of its content. Individual drafts on the DAWN problem statement and requirements call for a standardized minimum structure; without one, emerging discovery formats risk each defining its own minimal metadata, with descriptors that do not interoperate across organizational or protocol boundaries.
This document proposes a procedure that derives what is minimal from the scope of the charter, applies it to the charter's three deployment contexts (a local network, an organization, and the domain of a cooperating party), and proposes the resulting elements and the minimal constraints that hold among them as an information model in the sense of RFC 3444. It considers this information both as a publisher provides it and as a client obtains it; a value can come from the discovery response, from context the client already has, or from binding rules. This document is input to the charter's architecture and protocol deliverables and a mapping target for existing discovery mechanisms.
